title: STAT3 inhibitors combined with retinol binding protein 4 complex ameliorate DEN-induced liver carcinogenesis in mice and induce apoptosis via GRP78/ATF6/CHOP signaling pathway.
authors: Wu, Danxiao; Dong, Jie; Li, Xiaotao; Yu, Guangshu; Deng, Wenjun; Xu, Xinyi; Liu, Jinhui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究STAT3抑制剂与RBP4复合物对肝癌的治疗作用，仅用分子对接初步验证结合，核心是湿实验药效与凋亡通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: Primary liver cancers are most commonly hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs), often developing in the context of chronic liver diseases. It is characterized by aggressive growth and a poor prognosis despite treatment efforts. Hence, this present study was conducted using STAT3 inhibitors (S3I) combined with Retinol-binding protein 4 (RBP4), a combination that was confirmed by molecular docking analysis with binding score - 7.0 kcal/mol. Additionally, S3I@RBP4 exhibited protective effects against diethylnitrosamine (DEN) induced liver carcinoma in mouse models. The anti-tumor potential against human HCC in HepG2 and Hep3B cells was examined using MTT assay, which demonstrated that the treatment works by inducing apoptosis and inhibiting cell proliferation. In vitro, S3I@RBP4 treatment effectively suppressed HepG2 and Hep3B cell proliferation and increased intracellular ROS accumulation. Remarkably, in vitro, S3I@RBP4 induced caspase-dependent apoptosis in HCC cells by activating the GRP78/ATF6/CHOP signaling pathway. Conversely, in vivo, it counteracted DEN-induced effects by mitigating hepatic oxidative stress, reducing oxidative DNA damage and decreasing tumor-specific markers. In vivo studies further confirmed that S3I@RBP4 treatment mitigated liver damage, inflammation, and proliferation in mice exposed to DEN. The study highlights the potential of S3I@RBP4 for DEN-induced liver cancer therapy in mice. Over time, treated mice showed that inhibited cancer proliferation in histological analyses, which suggests that S3I@RBP4 is a promising candidate with chemotherapeutic potential against HCC. This work presents S3I@RBP4 as a safe and effective therapeutic option for liver cancer.
abstract_zh: 原发性肝癌最常见的是肝细胞癌（HCCs），通常发生在慢性肝病的背景下。其特征是侵袭性生长，且尽管经过治疗，预后仍然较差。因此，本研究采用STAT3抑制剂（S3I）与视黄醇结合蛋白4（RBP4）联合使用，该组合通过分子对接分析确认，结合评分为-7.0 kcal/mol。此外，S3I@RBP4在小鼠模型中表现出对二乙基亚硝胺（DEN）诱导的肝癌的保护作用。通过MTT实验检测了其对人类HCC HepG2和Hep3B细胞的抗肿瘤潜力，结果表明该治疗通过诱导凋亡和抑制细胞增殖发挥作用。在体外，S3I@RBP4处理有效抑制了HepG2和Hep3B细胞的增殖，并增加了细胞内ROS积累。值得注意的是，在体外，S3I@RBP4通过激活GRP78/ATF6/CHOP信号通路诱导HCC细胞中caspase依赖性凋亡。相反，在体内，它通过减轻肝脏氧化应激、减少氧化性DNA损伤和降低肿瘤特异性标志物来抵消DEN诱导的效应。体内研究进一步证实，S3I@RBP4处理减轻了暴露于DEN的小鼠的肝损伤、炎症和增殖。该研究强调了S3I@RBP4在DEN诱导的小鼠肝癌治疗中的潜力。随着时间的推移，组织学分析显示处理过的小鼠癌症增殖受到抑制，这表明S3I@RBP4是治疗HCC的具有化疗潜力的有前景候选药物。本研究将S3I@RBP4呈现为一种安全有效的肝癌治疗选择。
